checked_sources: Independent bounded checker independent_checks_1434.py, implicit primitive H(F)=F-Blog(1+F/B), random and multiblock checks
correctness.rationale: The capacity K(1+B/F) decreases in F, with finite bounded flux min(r,capacity) continuous at F=0. A high-flow clock z=int ds/g_h(s) turns high rate into translation; the low-rate clock has nondecreasing w(z)=g_ell/g_h, so low-flow derivative with respect to start is w(Psi_v(z))/w(z)>=1. This proves high-before-low interchange and its strict interval exactly F_h<F<F_ell. Before F_h both blocks infiltrate their stated rates; the strict iff boundaries reduce to F0<F_ell and F0+hu+ell v>F_h. Monotone scalar flows preserve prefix comparisons under any suffix, adjacent block interchanges sort arbitrary finite step functions; the flux is 1-Lipschitz in r in L1 and rearrangements are L1-contractive, extending to essentially bounded measurable rates. Independent implicit Green-Ampt primitive root solving checked 1000 two-block random sets and 250 random multiblock sorts, without substituting sampling for proof.
residual_risks: The model explicitly excludes ponding/surface storage and interstorm relaxation; strict iff proven only two positive rates.

checked_sources: Pinned RESULT.md high-clock comparison and exact capacity threshold
value.rationale: For uncertain intrastorm timing but a fixed rainfall intensity histogram, the theorem determines exact worst and best modeled infiltration and runoff. Its two-bin sharp equality region identifies when temporal ordering is physically immaterial in this model. The nonlinear transition through the capacity thresholds is a motivated structural comparison rather than trivial monotonicity in total volume.
residual_risks: This is a deliberately simplified instantaneous-runoff single-front model, not a universal hydrological rule.

final_claim: For scalar no-detention Green-Ampt infiltration F'=min(r(t),K(1+B/F)), bounded measurable nonnegative r over fixed T, descending equimeasurable rainfall intensity maximizes terminal F and ascending minimizes; for two strictly unequal positive blocks h>ell with positive durations u,v, strict high-first improvement holds iff h>K, F0<F_ell (infinite when ell<=K), and F0+hu+ell v>F_h, with exact equality otherwise.
limitations: Only essentially bounded nonnegative rainfall, F0>=0, T>0, K,B>0 and no storage/redistribution.
Two-block strictness requires positive distinct rates and durations; no arbitrary multiblock strict iff asserted.
